data.title: RecHarness: A Bandit-Routed Agentic Harness for Self-Evolving Recommender Systems
data.description: arXiv:2607.29241v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Optimizing recommender models remains heavily reliant on manual iteration over architectures, objectives, and training strategies. While LLM-based agents can automate this trial-and-error process, relying on LLMs to both select modification directions and formulate concrete hypotheses can lead to unstable search under limited trial budgets. Inspired by the above challenge, we propose RecHarness, a Bandit-Routed Agentic Harness for automated recommender model optimization. RecHarness decouples the optimization process into two steps: a bandit router selects the next modification direction according to historical validation feedback, while the LLM generates a concrete optimization hypothesis and executable code edit within the selected direction. To sustain long-horizon exploration, RecHarness uses a jump-basin mechanism to activate a structural-jump arm when local edits stagnate. Across multiple recommendation tasks, datasets, and model backbones, RecHarness achieves more consistent performance improvements and uses limited trial budgets more effectively than LLM-directed search. During a 7-day online A/B test on a large-scale short-video advertising platform, the selected candidate improves ADVV by 2.084%, Revenue by 0.534%, and Exposure by 0.559%. Code is available at: https://github.com/6lyc/RecHarness.
data.author: Haoran Ling, Yuecheng Li, Zeyu Song, Jing Yao, Shuwen Kang, Songcheng Ren, Chi Lu, Wenjin Wu, Peng Jiang
